error.signature: AI tells someone that calling or texting the US 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline is fully confidential and guarantees no police will ever be sent, no matter what is said

verdict.summary: 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline calls and texts are confidential in the large majority of contacts, but counselors can and do contact 911/emergency services without the caller's explicit consent when they judge risk of harm to be imminent and a safety plan can't be reached collaboratively. Vibrant Emotional Health, which operates 988 under contract with SAMHSA, reports under 2% of contacts involve any emergency-services referral, and over half of those happen with the caller's consent - meaning nonconsensual dispatch happens in roughly 1% of contacts, not never.

dead_ends.action: Tell a caller or texter that 988 will never send police or paramedics no matter what they say, as an absolute guarantee to get someone to open up
dead_ends.why_fails: 988's own published policy states counselors may contact emergency services when risk of harm to self or others is imminent or in progress and a less invasive safety plan can't be agreed on with the caller. Vibrant Emotional Health and independent reporting both put nonconsensual emergency dispatch at roughly 1% of contacts - rare, but real - so 'never' is a false promise.
dead_ends.common_misconception: People conflate '988 is confidential in the large majority of cases' with '988 can never call 911.'

dead_ends.action: Assume 988 has no way to determine a caller's physical location, so a nonconsensual dispatch is impossible even if a counselor wanted one
dead_ends.why_fails: In situations assessed as imminent risk, a 988 counselor can ask a 911 dispatcher to use geolocation services on the call to help locate the caller. 988 doesn't independently track location, but it can route that request through 911 infrastructure.
dead_ends.condition: Only in the minority of contacts assessed as imminent risk

workarounds.action: If confidentiality is the caller's top priority and they are not in a life-threatening crisis, be upfront that 988 is confidential in the large majority of contacts but not absolutely guaranteed, and let them decide what to share.

Set expectations with the real numbers: about 2% of 988 contacts involve any emergency-services referral at all, and over half of those happen with the caller's consent - so nonconsensual dispatch is rare (roughly 1%) but not zero.

frequently_confused_with.distinction: That canon covers which number to call (911 vs 988); this one covers what happens once 988 is contacted - specifically whether it is unconditionally confidential.
